NCU28076.question: $\ce{C6H5-C(CH3)2-Br}$ in aqueous ethanol gives an acidic solution, whereas $p$-$\ce{Br-C6H4-CH(CH3)2}$ in aqueous ethanol gives a neutral solution. The reason is
NCU28076.option1: both compounds hydrolyse, but HBr formed from the second one is neutralised by the ring
NCU28076.option2: $\ce{C6H5C(CH3)2Br}$ ionises easily ($S_N1$, stable 3° benzylic carbocation) and releases HBr, whereas Br on the benzene ring is not replaced because the C–Br bond has partial double bond character

NCU28076.correct_option: $\ce{C6H5C(CH3)2Br}$ ionises easily ($S_N1$, stable 3° benzylic carbocation) and releases HBr, whereas Br on the benzene ring is not replaced because the C–Br bond has partial double bond character
